1→# Phase 26 structured integration evidence — 2026-07-11
2→
3→## Outcome
4→
5→Phase 26 adds explicit `structured` integration while preserving `ff-only` as the default. Baton
6→never uses main as a merge workspace. It pins clean main and the accepted worker result, creates a
7→detached stage under `.baton/integrate/`, performs a real Git three-way merge, and invokes an
8→injected Mergiraf-class resolver only for unresolved regular text paths. Each resolver call sees
9→one bounded temporary conflict file in an isolated directory rather than the staging repository.
10→
11→Missing tools, non-success or unknown status, parse fallback, unsupported paths, oversized input
12→or output, timeout, invalid UTF-8, remaining conflict markers, unmerged index entries, and
13→`git diff --check` failure refuse. A candidate must have the exact main/result parents. Baton then
14→runs the immutable pinned primary command in a distinct fresh worktree at that candidate. Only an
15→observed pass may guard a final main fast-forward, which rechecks that main is still clean and at
16→the pinned SHA.
17→
18→The integration record pins before/result/merge-base/stage/after identities, per-path classes,
19→resolver evidence, and the fresh verdict. Refusal retains the accepted result ref. Post-effect
20→coordination failure poisons; restart replay does not invent success. Startup reconciliation
21→removes orphan stages because an old candidate without a live fresh verdict has no authority.
22→
23→## Validation
24→
25→- Numbered contract: `spec/phase26/structured-merge.md` (SM1–SM10).
26→- Focused gate: 14/14.
27→- Existing acceptance/worktree plus Phase 26 gate: 69/69.
28→- Canonical owned suite: 766/766; suite root reaped.
29→- Reds cover unavailable resolver, marker retention, parse fallback, deployment file ceiling,
30→  resolver isolation, clean divergent three-way merge, false-clean syntax failure, dirty main,
31→  main-advance race, post-main authority failure/replay, and orphan-stage reconciliation.
32→- The external `mergiraf` binary is absent on this host. Production invocation is implemented
33→  with fixed no-shell `mergiraf solve <path>` argv, bounded time/output, and a minimal environment;
34→  tests use an injected executor and do not claim a live external-tool pass.
35→
36→## Recursive Baton scope review
37→
38→Exact `grok-4.5` and `grok-composer-2.5-fast` independently reviewed the scope concurrently through
39→Baton before implementation. Both provider identities were observed on distinct overlapping PIDs,
40→both reports were freshly verified, both workers were normally killed, and every process,
41→worktree, runtime, and branch was reaped. Both converged on isolated staging, an injected external
42→resolver, mandatory fresh verification, and an explicit ban on CPG/fingerprint merge authority.
43→The reports and lifecycle ledger are under
44→`docs/reference/evidence/phase26-structured-merge-scope-grok-review-2026-07-11/`.
45→
46→A second concurrent exact-model pass reviewed the committed implementation. Grok 4.5 found that
47→NUL-containing Git-binary conflicts could reach a cooperative resolver; Composer found a
48→delimiter-free marker evasion and ambient `GIT_*` control of local Git subprocesses. All three now
49→have reds. Binary conflicts refuse before resolver invocation, marker scanning rejects any run of
50→seven or more diff3 marker characters at line start, and local worktree Git strips ambient Git
51→variables, disables system/global configuration, and disables hooks for merge/commit. The initial
52→implementation reports and complete kill/reap ledger are under
53→`docs/reference/evidence/phase26-structured-merge-implementation-grok-review-2026-07-11/`.
54→
55→The first concurrent final retry also exposed an operator-cleanup hazard: while recovering disk
56→headroom, an overbroad stale-log pattern deleted the active runner log directory. Baton poisoned
57→immediately, made no review claim, and reaped all provider and Git ownership. The runner now marks
58→its active log root `ACTIVE_DO_NOT_REAP` and supports exact single-model closure runs for bounded
59→disk environments. That failed evidence is retained under
60→`docs/reference/evidence/phase26-structured-merge-final-grok-review-2026-07-11/`.
61→
62→Sequential exact-model closure was then used without weakening model identity or lifecycle gates.
63→Grok 4.5 found no remaining actionable defect after the first correction set. Composer found one
64→adjacent asymmetry: binary NUL was rejected before resolver invocation but not if injected into
65→the resolver output. Output bytes now receive the same `structured_binary_conflict` gate before
66→UTF-8/marker acceptance, and one red exercises both pre- and post-resolver binary refusal. The
67→pre-correction reports are retained under
68→`docs/reference/evidence/phase26-structured-merge-closure-grok45-2026-07-11/` and
69→`docs/reference/evidence/phase26-structured-merge-closure-composer-2026-07-11/`.
70→
71→Composer's next exact-model pass found that lexical conflict-path confinement was not sufficient
72→against a parent directory swapped to an escaping symlink between the pre-resolver read and the
73→post-resolver write. Baton now canonical-realpath confines the conflict before reading and requires
74→the path to retain that exact canonical identity immediately before writing. A hostile timed swap
75→refuses `structured_unsupported_path`, leaves main pinned, and leaves the external sentinel
76→untouched. That report and lifecycle proof are under
77→`docs/reference/evidence/phase26-structured-merge-definitive-composer-2026-07-11/`.
78→
79→The next closure attempt showed that even a single reviewer could exhaust the host while the trust
80→gate checked out every historical evidence ledger merely to verify one report. Baton still killed
81→and reaped the provider, but the report could not be trusted. `freshVerifySandbox` now supports an
82→explicit list of safe relative literal paths, creates a no-checkout detached worktree, applies a
83→non-cone exact sparse projection, and then verifies the same full commit identity. The recursive
84→review runner selects only its exact report paths; ordinary product verification stays full by
85→default. A worktree red proves the report is present, unrelated files are absent, the exact commit
86→is checked out, and traversal is refused. The failed full-checkout evidence is retained under
87→`docs/reference/evidence/phase26-structured-merge-sparse-red-composer-2026-07-11/`.
88→
89→The first sparse retry then exposed an unrelated but live Baton control seam: an approval raced a
90→closed Grok stdin and Node emitted an unhandled asynchronous `EPIPE`. `_writeRaw` is now an owned
91→promise-based delivery, stdin has an error consumer, request RPCs reject their exact pending call,
92→and steer/interrupt/approval return refused delivery instead of emitting false success. Approval
93→waits are consumed only after the response enters the wire. The 32/32 Grok adapter gate includes a
94→closed-pipe red and the canonical suite remains green.
95→
96→## Honest boundary
97→
98→This is syntax-aware structured integration, not semantic merge. Mergiraf can reduce textual
99→conflicts but cannot prove behavior. Baton's fresh pinned check can still be weak. CPG deltas and
100→behavioral fingerprints may later escalate review or refusal, but there is deliberately no hook by
101→which either can advance main or skip verification. True data/control-flow merge remains a
102→catalogued research bet pending an adoptable external engine, measured residual demand after this
103→rung, and an evidence-backed false-clean advantage.
104→

# Phase 26 structured integration evidence — 2026-07-11

## Outcome

Phase 26 adds explicit `structured` integration while preserving `ff-only` as the default. Baton
never uses main as a merge workspace. It pins clean main and the accepted worker result, creates a
detached stage under `.baton/integrate/`, performs a real Git three-way merge, and invokes an
injected Mergiraf-class resolver only for unresolved regular text paths. Each resolver call sees
one bounded temporary conflict file in an isolated directory rather than the staging repository.

Missing tools, non-success or unknown status, parse fallback, unsupported paths, oversized input
or output, timeout, invalid UTF-8, remaining conflict markers, unmerged index entries, and
`git diff --check` failure refuse. A candidate must have the exact main/result parents. Baton then
runs the immutable pinned primary command in a distinct fresh worktree at that candidate. Only an
observed pass may guard a final main fast-forward, which rechecks that main is still clean and at
the pinned SHA.

The integration record pins before/result/merge-base/stage/after identities, per-path classes,
resolver evidence, and the fresh verdict. Refusal retains the accepted result ref. Post-effect
coordination failure poisons; restart replay does not invent success. Startup reconciliation
removes orphan stages because an old candidate without a live fresh verdict has no authority.

## Validation

- Numbered contract: `spec/phase26/structured-merge.md` (SM1–SM10).
- Focused gate: 14/14.

  tests use an injected executor and do not claim a live external-tool pass.

## Recursive Baton scope review

Baton before implementation. Both provider identities were observed on distinct overlapping PIDs,
both reports were freshly verified, both workers were normally killed, and every process,

resolver, mandatory fresh verification, and an explicit ban on CPG/fingerprint merge authority.
The reports and lifecycle ledger are under
`docs/reference/evidence/phase26-structured-merge-scope-grok-review-2026-07-11/`.

A second concurrent exact-model pass reviewed the committed implementation. Grok 4.5 found that
NUL-containing Git-binary conflicts could reach a cooperative resolver; Composer found a
delimiter-free marker evasion and ambient `GIT_*` control of local Git subprocesses. All three now
have reds. Binary conflicts refuse before resolver invocation, marker scanning rejects any run of
seven or more diff3 marker characters at line start, and local worktree Git strips ambient Git
variables, disables system/global configuration, and disables hooks for merge/commit. The initial
implementation reports and complete kill/reap ledger are under
`docs/reference/evidence/phase26-structured-merge-implementation-grok-review-2026-07-11/`.

the resolver output. Output bytes now receive the same `structured_binary_conflict` gate before

`docs/reference/evidence/phase26-structured-merge-closure-composer-2026-07-11/`.

# Adversarial dogfood — Phase 26 SM1–SM10 @ bb991a4

**Pin:** `bb991a4` (*Poison structured post-effect ambiguity*).  
**Sources (code over prose):** `spec/phase26/structured-merge.md`; `impl/src/structured-merge.mjs`; `impl/src/worktree.mjs` (stage/finalize/reconcile); `impl/src/coordinator.mjs` (`integrate`, poison, replay); `impl/src/index.mjs` (worktree manager, pins); `impl/test/phase26-structured-merge.test.mjs`; `docs/handoff/evidence/phase26-structured-merge-2026-07-11.md`; Phase 11 integration/replay (`impl/test/phase11-acceptance-integration.test.mjs` AC5/CK9).

## Decision

**No actionable SM1–SM10 implementation defect remains at bb991a4.**

The commit closes the concrete post-effect authority hole: after a successful main fast-forward, `afterSha` / cleanliness failures are tagged `structured_post_effect_inconsistent` + `postEffect: true` (`worktree.mjs` `postEffectMergeError`, `finalizeStructuredIntegration`), and the coordinator records `integration.incomplete` then `_poisonIntegration` instead of `integration.refused` (`coordinator.mjs` integrate catch + `_poisonIntegration`). Pre-effect failures still refuse without moving main; operational success + coordination integration batch remain the only replayable success (`integrationAuthority` + replay `integration.completed` gate). Residual gaps are either explicit non-goals (true semantic merge, live Mergiraf binary, CPG/fingerprint authority) or catastrophic Git subprocess failure modes outside the numbered contract’s testable surface—not ship-blocking SM defects.

| Seam | Verdict |
|------|---------|
| SM1 injected resolver | **Hold** — fixed `mergiraf solve <path>`, `shell: false`, bounded time/output; tests inject executor |
| SM2 main ≠ stage | **Hold** — stage under `.baton/integrate/`; main only FF at finalize |
| SM3 exact identities | **Hold** — before/result/base/stage; parent pair checked at stage + finalize; dirty/advance refuse |
| SM4 fail-closed classify | **Hold** — binary/symlink/markers/fallback/ceilings/unmerged/`diff --check` refuse typed |
| SM5 immutable candidate | **Hold** — two-parent commit only after full resolve + check; not main |
| SM6 fresh verify | **Hold** — distinct verify worktree at `stageSha`; pinned primary; `requireRedGreen: false` |
| SM7 one guarded main update | **Hold** — clean + `HEAD==beforeSha` then `merge --ff-only --no-verify`; hooks disabled |
| SM8 replay/authority | **Hold** — completed only via op log + `completeIntegration` batch; post-effect poisons; incomplete ≠ success |
| SM9 cleanup/retention | **Hold** — stage/verify reaped success/refuse/throw; reconcile sweeps orphans; pin release only on success |
| SM10 semantic boundary | **Hold** — no CPG/fingerprint path in `integrate`; research tombstone in spec only |

## Proposed numbered contract

Operational restatement of SM1–SM10 as enforced by this tree (not a rewrite of the spec):

1. **SM1** Production `MergirafResolver` invokes `execFile(binary, ['solve', relativePath], { shell: false, env: PATH/LANG/LC_ALL only })` with deployment `timeoutMs` / `maxOutputBytes` / `maxFileBytes`. Outcomes: `resolved` only on exit 0 + `solved N conflict` without parse-fallback text; else `parse_fallback` / `unresolved` / `unknown` or typed `structured_tool_*`. Never map textual fallback to structured success.
2. **SM2** `stageStructuredIntegration` requires clean main, pins `beforeSha`, creates detached worktree at `.baton/integrate/<taskId>-<hex>` from `beforeSha`. All merge/resolve/index/commit run there. Main HEAD/index/worktree unchanged until SM7.
3. **SM3** Stage freezes `beforeSha`, full `resultSha`, `mergeBaseSha`, `stageSha`, conflict paths/classes. Refuse: invalid result, result already ancestor of main, dirty main, main ≠ `beforeSha` at finalize, parent pair ≠ `(beforeSha, resultSha)`.
4. **SM4** Clean three-way → `clean_textual`. Each `diff-filter=U` regular text path → isolated temp file + resolver; success class `structured_resolved` only after NUL-free UTF-8, no conflict-marker run of 7+ `<=>|` chars, path realpath stable, `git add`. Binary/delete/escape/fallback/unknown/unmerged/`git diff --check` → typed refuse; stage reaped.
5. **SM5** Candidate is `git commit` of the fully resolved stage with exact two parents; object alone is not acceptance.
6. **SM6** Before main moves: `createVerifyWorktree(taskId-structured-merge, stageSha)` + referee on `task.brief.verification` with `requireRedGreen/Coverage/Mutation: false`. Fail → `structured_verification_failed`, reap stage+verify, retain result pin, main unchanged.
7. **SM7** Only after SM6 accept: recheck clean + `HEAD==beforeSha` + parents, then `git -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null merge --no-verify --ff-only stageSha`. Success record includes before/result/base/stage/after, classes, resolver identity, verdict. No push/deploy.
8. **SM8** Replayable success iff operational `integration.completed` **and** `coordination.integrationAuthority` (promoted Decision + driver.completed + accepted artifact batch). Asymmetric decision/candidate/resolver report cannot reconstruct success. After Git effect boundary: append `integration.incomplete` + poison (`structured_post_effect_inconsistent`); never `integration.refused`; never silent hard-reset of user HEAD.
9. **SM9** `removeStructuredIntegration` / `removeVerifyWorktree` on every integrate outcome; `reconcile` force-removes all `.baton/integrate/*` (no resume without fresh verdict). Success releases `refs/baton/results/<sha>`; refusal/incomplete retain pin. No stage branch.
10. **SM10** CPG/behavior APIs are not consulted in `integrate`. True semantic merge remains out of scope until an external engine proves false-clean advantage; redirect to structured + fresh verify.

## Red tests and proof

Concrete sequences grounded in source (not worker prose). Codes cite implementation lines by path.

### SM1 — resolver injection / no-shell
